intro: Hawker-centre food blending Malay, Chinese and Indian cooking: coconut, sambal and wok smoke, with plenty of overlap between the two countries.
flavours: Sambal, coconut milk, belacan (shrimp paste), pandan, lemongrass
hk: Malaysian and Singaporean cafés across Hong Kong serve laksa, Hainanese chicken rice and kaya toast.

dishes.name: Nasi lemak
dishes.what: Malaysia's national dish: coconut rice with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.

dishes.name: Hainanese chicken rice
dishes.what: Poached silky chicken with rice cooked in chicken fat and stock, plus chilli and ginger sauces.

dishes.name: Laksa
dishes.what: Spicy noodle soup; curry laksa has a coconut broth, Penang assam laksa a sour fish one.

dishes.name: Char kway teow
dishes.what: Flat rice noodles stir-fried in a smoking wok with prawns, cockles, Chinese sausage and egg.

dishes.name: Satay
dishes.what: Skewers of marinated grilled meat with peanut sauce.

dishes.name: Roti canai
dishes.what: Flaky, stretched flatbread griddled until crisp, dipped in dhal or curry (roti prata in Singapore).

dishes.name: Chilli crab
dishes.what: Singapore's signature: mud crab in a sweet, spicy tomato-chilli sauce, mopped up with fried buns.

dishes.name: Bak kut teh
dishes.what: 'Meat bone tea': pork ribs in a peppery or herbal broth.

dishes.name: Kaya toast
dishes.what: Toast with coconut-egg jam and a slab of cold butter, with soft-boiled eggs and kopi.
